title: Finite coproduct decomposition of an object
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category, $I$ a set and $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ a family of objects of $\mathcal C$. A *coproduct* of the family is an object $X$ with morphisms $\iota_i:X_i\to X$ ($i\in I$) such that for every object $T$ and every family of morphisms $t_i:X_i\to T$ there is exactly one morphism $t:X\to T$ with $t\circ\iota_i=t_i$ for all $i$; that is, $X$ is the colimit of the diagram indexed by the discrete category on $I$. An object $X$ *is a finite coproduct of* objects with a property $P$ if there are a finite set $I$ (possibly empty), objects $X_i$ ($i\in I$) having $P$, and morphisms $\iota_i:X_i\to X$ making $X$ a coproduct of $(X_i)_{i\in I}$. For $I=\emptyset$ this says that $X$ is initial ([def-galois-initial-mono]).
